paper_metadata.title: The Lie Algebra of XY-mixer Topologies and Warm Starting QAOA for Constrained Optimization

summary: The paper analyzes the dynamical Lie algebras of different XY‑mixer topologies in QAOA and proposes a warm‑start training strategy where a restricted polynomial‑size DLA circuit is pretrained before enabling the full exponential‑size ansatz. Numerical simulations using PennyLane on portfolio optimization (SP500), graph partitioning, and sparsest k‑subgraph instances with 12–16 qubits and depths up to p≈40 show that warm‑started multi‑angle QAOA significantly improves approximation ratio and success probability compared to random initialization.

experiments.description: Multi-angle QAOA with XY-mixer warm-starting on portfolio optimization instances (SP500, n=12/14/16 assets, k=n/2 selection).

algorithm.variant: multi-angle QAOA with warm-start and restricted-pretraining on polynomial-size DLA
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 100 steps pretraining on restricted ansatz, then 100 steps refinement on full ansatz

hyperparameters.phase_separators: RZ and RZZ terms in full circuit

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform [0, 2π] for restricted ansatz; transferred restricted optimum to full circuit with RZZ angles initialized to 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variable x_i indicates whether asset i is selected; exactly k=n/2 assets chosen
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x -p^T x + q x^T C x subject to |x| = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: XY-mixer preserves Hamming weight; Dicke-state initialization; no penalty terms in main warm-start circuit
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = H_p + q H_covar, with H_p = -\sum_i p_i \sigma_i^1 and H_covar = \sum_{i,j} C_{ij} \sigma_i^1 \sigma_j^1

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over publicly available SP500 monthly data; select k=n/2 assets maximizing return and minimizing risk

dataset_specification.description: Publicly available trading data from 2010 to 2018; top-performing stocks selected per month; monthly returns and covariance matrices constructed

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily returns computed as (q_i^a - q_{i-1}^a)/q_{i-1}^a; monthly average return and covariance computed from daily samples; top n stocks selected by average return per month; k=n/2 chosen
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Median performance over 10 random initializations; ribbons show lower and upper quartiles; evaluated across 84 monthly instances

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical construction of returns vector and covariance matrix from SP500 data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select best parameters by approximation ratio and success probability

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: warm-start begins with better approximation ratio and converges more smoothly than random initialization

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical optimization baseline or quantum speedup claim is reported; the paper compares warm-started QAOA against random initialization only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Warm-start training on polynomial-size DLA followed by refinement on full ansatz; no explicit asymptotic runtime given for the optimization task
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: No explicit asymptotic classical baseline given for the optimization task

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiments performed on classical simulator with ≤16 qubits.
limiting_factors: Only classical simulation of circuits (≤16 qubits).
No comparison against classical optimization algorithms (e.g., CPLEX, heuristics).
Performance metric compares warm-start vs random initialization, not quantum vs classical methods.

notes: Hardware is not specified beyond use of PennyLane; treated as not specified rather than inferred simulator.
Circuit depth p and parameter counts are explicitly given in the Methods; p-depth up to 40 appears in figures, and p=10 is used in training plots.
No gate counts, shots, or transpiled depth are reported.
Authors do not claim quantum advantage; experiments only compare different QAOA initialization strategies.
No classical baseline for portfolio optimization performance is reported.

experiments.description: Comparison between shared-angle QAOA (SA-QAOA) and multi-angle QAOA (MA-QAOA) with and without warm starting on portfolio optimization instances.

algorithm.variant: shared-angle vs multi-angle QAOA comparison with warm-start initialization

key_results: Supplementary Figure S1 shows MA-QAOA consistently outperforms SA-QAOA in both approximation ratio and success probability.
Warm-start initialization improves both SA-QAOA and MA-QAOA performance relative to random initialization.
Experiments conducted for n = 12, 14, 16 assets using SP500 portfolio optimization instances.
